memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "I will give you every place where you set your foot, as I promised Moses. Your territory will extend from the desert to Lebanon, and from the great river, the Euphrates — all the Hittite country — to the Mediterranean Sea in the west." — Josh 1:3-4 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God had already promised this land generations earlier to Abraham. Now He confirms the boundaries to Joshua. This was a specific national promise to Israel about a specific piece of land — it is not a promise that Christians today will receive property wherever we walk. We must be honest about that, or we twist Scripture into something it never said.

Yet there is a timeless truth here that belongs to us. God does not promise blessing in the abstract; He promises to meet His people as they actually step out in obedience. The land was already given "as I promised," but Israel still had to set their feet down and walk. Faith is not passive waiting; it is trusting God enough to move.

The promises God gives us in Christ are even greater than land. He has given us forgiveness, adoption, and an inheritance that can never perish (1 Pet 1:4). But like Israel, we take hold of what is ours by walking forward in faith, not by standing still.

God's character is the same across every generation: He keeps His word. What He promised Abraham, He fulfilled. What He promises in Christ, He will complete.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Where is God asking you to "set your foot" — to obey before you see the full outcome?
2. Are you waiting passively for something God has told you to walk toward?
3. What has God already secured for you in Christ that you have not yet taken hold of?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that You always keep Your word. Give me faith not just to believe Your promises but to walk forward in them. Amen.
